name: Automatic Dustbin
description: Touchless waste bin that automatically opens its lid when hands or trash approach, using distance sensing and servo rotation.
overview: Reuses common maker parts to build a hygienic touchless lid mechanism. The ultrasonic sensor triggers the servo arm by 90 degrees when an object is detected within 15 cm.
buildSteps: Mount the ultrasonic sensor facing forward on the dustbin lid hinge.
Attach the servo horn to the lid flapper using a rigid wire arm.
Wire HC-SR04 Trig to Pin 9, Echo to Pin 10, and Servo signal to Pin 6 on the Arduino.
Add a 220-ohm current limiting resistor to the LED and connect to Pin 13 as a status indicator.
Flash the lid actuation firmware with calibrated distance threshold (15cm).

name: Smart Parking Indicator
description: Monitors parking slot occupancy in real time and alerts drivers using dual IR sensors, visual LEDs, and audible buzzers.
overview: Deploys paired infrared sensors at bay entrances to identify vehicle presence, lighting green/red status LEDs and beeping if bay is over-occupied.
buildSteps: Position IR Sensor 1 at Bay A and IR Sensor 2 at Bay B facing the vehicle approach path.
Connect sensor digital outputs to Arduino Pins 2 and 3.
Wire green LED to Pin 4 (Empty) and red LED to Pin 5 (Occupied).
Connect the active buzzer to Pin 8 for entry acknowledgment audio chimes.
Test threshold pots on the IR modules under ambient lighting.

name: Automatic Night Lamp
description: Energy-conserving lighting fixture that detects ambient darkness and turns on soft illumination automatically.
overview: Uses a voltage divider circuit with a light-dependent resistor (LDR) to sample twilight levels and illuminate dual high-efficiency LEDs without manual switching.
buildSteps: Form a voltage divider using the LDR and a 10k resistor connected between 5V and GND.
Tap the divider midpoint into Arduino Analog Pin A0.
Connect two LEDs in parallel with current-limiting resistors to digital Pin 11.
Calibrate the twilight threshold in code to smoothly toggle lights as room light drops.
Enclose in a frosted diffuser repurposed from plastic packaging.

name: Obstacle Detection System
description: Proximity warning module that emits progressive audio and visual pulses as obstacles get dangerously close.
overview: Measures time-of-flight sound waves. As objects breach the 30cm and 10cm safety envelopes, buzzer frequency and LED blinking speed up.
buildSteps: Connect ultrasonic Trig to Pin 7 and Echo to Pin 8.
Connect caution LED to Pin 4, critical warning LED to Pin 5.
Attach buzzer to Pin 6 using PWM frequency output.
Implement step-wise pulse interval mapping relative to measured distance.

name: Smart Door System
description: Hands-free automated doorway lock latch that rotates when legitimate human motion is sensed in the entry corridor.
overview: Detects infrared body heat motion using the PIR sensor. Triggers an entry chime and drives a high-torque servo mechanism to unlatch a cabinet or door.
buildSteps: Mount PIR sensor above eye level to prevent false triggers.
Connect PIR signal pin to Arduino digital interrupt Pin 2.
Connect servo control lead to Pin 9 with 5V external power rail.
Wire buzzer to Pin 7 for lock confirmation feedback.
Program a 5-second automatic re-latch timer after entry.

name: Automatic Fan Controller
description: Smart climate controller that reads ambient temperature and drives a cooling fan via relay whenever threshold limits are exceeded.
overview: Monitors room heat using the DHT11 sensor. If temperature breaches 28°C, the relay triggers to switch power to an electric fan motor.
buildSteps: Connect DHT11 signal pin to Arduino Pin 4 with a 10k pull-up resistor.
Connect relay input control pin to Pin 8.
Route the DC motor positive power rail through the relay Common and Normally Open (NO) terminals.
Write hysteresis loop logic (turn on at 28°C, shut down at 26°C) to prevent rapid relay fluttering.

name: Temperature Monitoring System
description: Desktop weather monitor that displays real-time ambient temperature and humidity metrics on a crisp alphanumeric display.
overview: Continuously polls temperature and humidity, formatting the environmental data into readable Celsius and %RH rows on a standard 1602 LCD.
buildSteps: Connect DHT11 data line to digital Pin 2.
Wire the LCD 16x2 data bus (or I2C adapter to SDA/SCL Pins A4/A5).
Add a 220-ohm resistor for LCD backlight power regulation.
Upload sketch utilizing the LiquidCrystal and DHT sensor libraries.
Tune refresh rates to update readings once every two seconds.

name: Motion Detection System
description: Perimeter intrusion detector that sounds an alarm and flashes warning lights immediately upon detecting human movement.
overview: A compact security module designed for doorways, sheds, or workshops to deter unauthorized presence using immediate sensory alerts.
buildSteps: Connect PIR output to Arduino Pin 2.
Connect alert LED to Pin 12 with a 330 ohm resistor.
Connect piezo buzzer to Pin 11.
Write loop code to sound 2kHz alarm beeps whenever the PIR output goes HIGH.
Mount in an enclosed housing pointing toward entrance paths.

name: Smart Light Controller
description: Dual-mode lighting switch allowing both automated ambient light triggering and manual push-button override.
overview: Combines an optical sensor with a tactile push button to operate home lighting relays smartly with manual override options.
buildSteps: Wire LDR voltage divider to Analog Pin A1.
Wire momentary push button to digital Pin 3 with internal pull-up.
Connect relay trigger terminal to digital Pin 7.
Program state machine with Auto/Manual toggle mode.

name: Digital Notice Board
description: Programmable digital signage device that cycles announcements, alerts, and schedules via push button controls.
overview: Employs an ESP32 microcontroller with an alphanumeric display to serve campus or workspace bulletin notifications with paginated navigation.
buildSteps: Connect LCD 16x2 via I2C to ESP32 Pins 21 (SDA) and 22 (SCL).
Connect Next and Prev buttons to Pins 18 and 19 with pull-down resistors.
Store notice messages in flash memory array.
Display messages with horizontal scrolling effect.

name: Water Level Indicator
description: Overhead tank water monitor that prevents overflow and wastage using multi-stage LED depth bars and an alert buzzer.
overview: Non-contact acoustic liquid measurement. Gauges distance to the water surface, mapping level to Low (Green), Medium (Yellow), and Full (Red + Buzzer).
buildSteps: Suspend the ultrasonic sensor on top of the reservoir pointing downward.
Wire green LED to Pin 2, yellow LED to Pin 3, red LED to Pin 4 with resistors.
Connect buzzer to Pin 5 for overflow prevention warning.
Calibrate full and empty tank depth in centimetres.

name: RFID Attendance Prototype
description: Contactless identification system that reads student or employee RFID cards, logs entry, and provides visual confirmation.
overview: Interrogates 13.56 MHz RFID tags using the SPI protocol. Displays the registered card holder's name and rings a positive acknowledgment chime.
buildSteps: Wire RC522 RFID reader to Arduino SPI pins (SCK 13, MISO 12, MOSI 11, SS 10, RST 9).
Connect LCD 16x2 via I2C to pins A4 and A5.
Wire buzzer to digital Pin 6 for tap audio feedback.
Program authorization lookup table containing valid UID hex strings.

name: Smart Parking System
description: Automated parking boom barrier that detects approaching vehicles, checks remaining space, and operates a servo gate.
overview: Coordinates entry and exit IR beams to tally occupied spots and swing a boom barrier servo when capacity is available.
buildSteps: Place IR Sensor 1 at entrance barrier, IR Sensor 2 at exit barrier.
Connect servo arm acting as boom gate to Pin 9.
Connect LCD display to report Available Slots counter.
Increment and decrement count dynamically based on tripped sensors.

name: Line Detection Robot electronics module project
description: Autonomous tracking core that processes dual ground IR reflections to steer differential drive DC motors along a contrast path.
overview: Core robotics navigation controller. Reads left and right black line reflectance and modulates PWM speeds to left and right drive motors.
buildSteps: Mount dual IR sensors 1cm above track surface spaced 2cm apart.
Connect sensor outputs to Pins A0 and A1.
Connect motor driver inputs (IN1-IN4) to Pins 5, 6, 9, 10.
Hook up left and right DC drive motors to driver output terminals.
Implement proportional steering control algorithm.

name: Home Automation Prototype
description: Wireless appliance switcher that pairs with smartphones over Bluetooth to control dual electrical loads remotely.
overview: Listens for serial commands from a paired mobile phone terminal to toggle lighting relays and indicator LEDs safely.
buildSteps: Connect HC-05 TX to Arduino RX (Pin 0) and HC-05 RX via resistor divider to TX (Pin 1).
Connect Relay 1 to Pin 7, Relay 2 to Pin 8.
Add status LEDs on Pins 12 and 13.
Parse incoming ASCII characters ('A' for on, 'a' for off) in serial handler.

name: Weather Monitoring Prototype
description: Compact micro-climate station utilizing an ESP8266 and precision DHT22 sensor to display barometric comfort levels on a sharp OLED screen.
overview: Compact environmental telemetry unit suited for balconies or greenhouses. Draws live readings with temperature, humidity, and heat index curves.
buildSteps: Connect SSD1306 OLED display via I2C (D1 = SCL, D2 = SDA).
Connect DHT22 data pin to D4 with a 4.7k pull-up resistor.
Program Adafruit SSD1306 and DHT libraries on the ESP8266.
Render sleek graphic temperature gauge on the OLED.

name: Smart Energy Monitor
description: Intelligent power socket monitor that tracks run-time hours and lets users switch appliance relay power via push button.
overview: Measures continuous device operation cycles and provides scheduled power cut-off to reduce vampire electronics power draw.
buildSteps: Connect 0.96 inch I2C OLED to ESP32 GPIO 21 and 22.
Connect relay trigger input to GPIO 15.
Wire tactile pushbutton to GPIO 4 configured with internal pull-up.
Display power state, active timer, and estimated watt-hours diverted.

name: Mini Security System
description: Keypad-armed safe box lock system with ultrasonic tripwire sensing and alarm sounding on invalid attempts.
overview: An electronic lockbox alarm that requires a 4-digit PIN code on the keypad to disarm before reaching inside the ultrasonic perimeter.
buildSteps: Wire 4x4 matrix keypad rows and columns to Arduino Pins 2 through 9.
Connect ultrasonic sensor to Pins 10 and 11.
Connect alarm buzzer to Pin 12.
Program arm/disarm passcode verification logic.

name: Smart Plant Watering Controller
description: Automated plant irrigation controller that measures soil dryness and dispenses water through a relay-switched pump.
overview: Prevents overwatering and plant drought. Probes soil conductivity and triggers a 5V submersible water pump when moisture drops below 35%.
buildSteps: Insert soil moisture sensor probes into plant pot root zone.
Connect analog sensor pin to Arduino A0.
Connect relay signal to Pin 7.
Power 5V mini DC pump through the relay contact.
Set calibration watering intervals to avoid water pooling.

name: mmWave Radar Smart Presence & Energy Controller
description: State-of-the-art human presence monitor that detects stationary breathing and micro-motion through 24GHz radar to automate room energy.
overview: Unlike PIR sensors that require walking movement, this 24GHz radar sensor detects stationary occupants even while sitting or sleeping, eliminating false light shutoffs.
buildSteps: Connect mmWave radar sensor UART TX/RX pins to ESP32 GPIO 16 and 17.
Wire 5V relay control line to GPIO 23 to switch room lighting.
Connect indicator status LED to GPIO 2 with current-limiting resistor.
Configure radar distance gates (0.75m to 4.5m) and sensitivity thresholds.
Upload logic to hold relay active during detected micro-motion presence.

name: mmWave Radar Perimeter Security Sentry
description: Through-wall perimeter intrusion sentry that measures intruder distance and approach velocity using microwave radar.
overview: Invisible motion tripwire that operates through non-metallic enclosures and darkness, showing exact target distance and sounding directional alarms.
buildSteps: Connect mmWave radar sensor output pin or UART to Arduino Pins 2 and 3.
Wire OLED display via I2C to Analog Pins A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL).
Connect alert piezo buzzer to PWM Pin 9.
Display real-time intruder distance meter on the OLED display.
Sound progressive frequency alarms when intruder enters within 2 meters.

name: LoRa Long-Range Agricultural Soil & Weather Station
description: Off-grid telemetry node that broadcasts soil moisture, temperature, and humidity up to 10 kilometers over sub-gigahertz LoRa radio.
overview: Enables smart farming across large acreage without cellular or Wi-Fi fees. Samples soil hygrometry and broadcasts encrypted telemetry packets every 15 minutes.
buildSteps: Wire LoRa SX1278 SPI bus (MISO 12, MOSI 11, SCK 13, NSS 10, DIO0 2) to Arduino.
Connect soil moisture sensor to Analog Pin A0.
Connect DHT22 temperature and humidity sensor to Digital Pin 4.
Flash LoRa packet transmission firmware configured to 433MHz or 868MHz.
Deploy in weatherproof housing with power optimization sleep cycles.

name: LoRa Off-Grid Emergency GPS Locator
description: Off-grid wearable survival beacon that acquires satellite coordinates and transmits SOS location packets over long-range LoRa radio.
overview: Provides vital emergency locating in wilderness or disaster zones where cellular towers fail, transmitting GPS coordinates over kilometres.
buildSteps: Connect NEO-6M GPS serial output (TX/RX) to ESP32 Serial2 (GPIO 16/17).
Wire LoRa module via SPI to ESP32 (MOSI 23, MISO 19, SCK 18, CS 5, DIO0 26).
Connect I2C OLED display to GPIO 21 and 22.
Parse NMEA GPS location sentences and package latitude/longitude into compact binary packets.
Transmit periodic beacon and display local satellite lock status on OLED.

name: LoRa Smart Home Central Receiver Gateway
description: Central receiver hub that collects telemetry from remote outdoor LoRa sensors and triggers home automation relays.
overview: Acts as the base station in a home network, receiving sensor packets from remote nodes and displaying status or driving power switches.
buildSteps: Connect LoRa receiver module to ESP32 SPI bus.
Connect LCD 16x2 over I2C to display real-time incoming packet data.
Connect relay switch to GPIO 15 to control home loads based on remote triggers.
Implement packet validation, RSSI signal strength tracking, and relay actuation.

name: Microwave Radar Speed & Motion Detector
description: Doppler radar speedometer that calculates approaching target velocity and displays speed metrics on a digital readout.
overview: Calculates speed by measuring frequency shift in reflected microwave radar signals, beeping and flashing when speed limits are exceeded.
buildSteps: Connect microwave radar sensor analog frequency output or serial to Arduino.
Wire TM1637 4-digit 7-segment display to digital Pins 4 (CLK) and 5 (DIO).
Connect warning buzzer to Pin 8.
Compute target velocity in km/h from Doppler frequency formula.
Display live velocity and trigger audio chirp on rapid acceleration.
